newsitem.title: FRANCE: France on verge of jobless trend reversal - Arthuis.
newsitem.headline: France on verge of jobless trend reversal - Arthuis.

text.p: French Finance Minister Jean Arthuis said on Tuesday, a day before March monthly jobless data is due, that unemployment was stabilising and should soon start turning downwards.

Arthuis told LCI television that, with a cautious official forecast of 2.3 percent growth in 1997, the economy would create 120,000-140,000 jobs this year but that it would take a few more months for a turnaround from a trend of increasing unemployment.

"My conviction is that with (1997) growth of 2.3 percent -- a cautious forecast -- we will create 120,000 to 140,000 jobs," he said in a face-to-face TV debate with Socialist former finance minister Michel Sapin.

"I know that for a few more months there will still be a considerable number of people entering the labour market for the first time. We know that in the coming months there will not be a downward turn in unemployment. But we are in a turnaround phase, we're on the eve of job creation which is estimated at 250,000 for 1998, he said.
"We're in a stabilisation phase," he added.
French March jobless data is due on Wednesday and economists are expecting the unemployment rate to remain at the current record level of 12.8 percent.
The figures are all the more sensitive because they come in the middle of the May 25/June 1 parliamentary election campaign.
Sapin reiterated a Socialist economic programme of creating 700,000 jobs with government backing, half of them in the public sector.

He also said the policy of the main opposition Socialist party was to boost consumer spending and that this came before the income tax drive started by the current centre-right government in its 1996 budget.
"The priority is not income tax cuts...it's stimulating consumer spending," Sapin said.
He said that if the Socialists were to cut tax, cuts in value added tax would be a priority.
